mechanism_narrative: Because WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both fell sharply in the most recent week, commuting-linked foot traffic will weaken further and pull RETAIL_REC down over the next four weeks. The signal is that retail follows aggregate daytime trip generation with a short lag.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall below its prior 4-week mean while WORKPLACES and TRANSIT remain at least 15 points below baseline for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in RESIDENTIAL time indicates more out-of-home activity, which should translate into more discretionary retail visits within one to two weeks. If people spend less time at home, they have more opportunities to shop and dine out.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below 12 points above baseline after being at or above 14 points the prior week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains flat or declines over the next 14 days after RESIDENTIAL drops below the stated threshold.

mechanism_narrative: When PARKS mobility rebounds strongly, discretionary trip-making broadens and spillovers support retail and restaurant visits over the next month. The effect is strongest after a sustained recovery from a recent trough.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises by at least 5 points week-on-week from a depressed level
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not exceed its last 4-week average by the end of four weeks despite a week-on-week PARKS increase of at least 5 points.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent deterioration in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES signals renewed restriction pressure or self-limiting behavior that reduces corridor shopping and in-person errands. Retail mobility should fall within one week of that combined drop.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT drops below -40 and WORKPLACES drops below -40 in the same week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises or stays above its prior week's level in the week after both proxies cross the threshold.

mechanism_narrative: When GROCERY_PHARM softens while RESIDENTIAL rises, households are consolidating trips and substituting away from discretionary shopping, which suppresses retail activity over the next two weeks. The mechanism fails if grocery runs remain elevated.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM declines week-on-week while RESIDENTIAL stays above 15 points
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 14 days despite the combined grocery decline and elevated residential time.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained recovery in TRANSIT after an acute trough should restore access to commercial areas and lift RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks. The retail response should appear after the transit trough stabilizes rather than immediately.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rebounds by at least 8 points from the prior week after a week below -40
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains below its last 4-week mean four weeks after TRANSIT rebounds by at least 8 points.

mechanism_narrative: If PARKS improve while GROCERY_PHARM is stable, the snapshot is consistent with seasonal outdoor substitution and local errand bundling that supports retail visits within one to four weeks. The effect depends on people spending more time in public leisure settings.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC declines over the next 28 days even though PARKS stays above its prior week and GROCERY_PHARM does not worsen.

mechanism_narrative: A regime-specific transit collapse combined with persistent workplace weakness implies access friction and fewer impulse shopping trips, so retail mobility should be lower over the next four weeks. This mechanism is strongest when the transit drop is abrupt rather than gradual.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls more than 10 points week-on-week while WORKPLACES remains below -30
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above its last 4-week mean within four weeks after the transit shock despite WORKPLACES staying below -30.
